summary: Frozen local-first architecture, CLI/config/result/helper contracts, conservative selection and lifecycle boundaries, plus 15 owned test-first tasks with a local-only legacy bootstrap barrier and A1-A14 traceability. No runtime code changed.
decisions: One account-derived SQLite coordinator, atomic FIFO all-resource admission, private per-run guard and cooperative process-group lifecycle; no daemon or per-TUI budget.
Guard facts remain provisional until group absence and caller finalization while charged; dead-caller recovery cannot manufacture a successful baseline.
Explicit source-to-test file groups and complete compatible native inventories; unknown inputs, changed policy/config, shared test dependencies and unresolved failures widen to full.
Native pytest bridge retains native configuration and serial without xdist; supported xdist controls and critical hook owners are validated before gateways.

Vitest 3.2.7 is the release acceptance target, with one initialized native instance, public configureVitest reporter append and exact test specifications; inspected 3.2.6 is not a patched support claim.
Go/Cargo retain bounded execution-only subsets; arbitrary wrappers require explicit exclusive best-effort profile rather than a guessed cap.
All arbitrary argv is withheld from default owned output; explicit reveal is labeled and unpersisted, raw child streams remain unchanged.
Static doctor, explicit bounded probes, generic ownership recipes and one installed guide do not launch agents, import repository code during inspection, or change TUI trust/config.
One shared contract catalog generates JSON schemas; bootstrap freezes records and helper signatures before independent writers. Sequential CLI ownership transfers avoid registration conflicts.
Legacy local contracts are mapped before explicit source/test deletion; installed live CLI, recovery tag, remote infrastructure and provisional worktree remain untouched.
review_preflight_dispositions: Added ptest changed alias and history test-or-file filter to match the approved CLI contract.
Defined auxiliary record fields, GroupObservation, typed Problem exception, internal RunResult admission sequence/input identities, and fixture helper aliases explicitly.
Distinguished ignored HOME/XDG from explicit unsupported PTEST location overrides, which fail visibly; bootstrap clears legacy-only overrides before candidate child invocation.
Fixture domains validate private directory ownership/device/inode/identity and contain every fixture project/output; normal evidence cannot be seeded from them.
Status is non-mutating; active admission drives recovery while status reports the computed ownership/recoverability view.
Adoption projects are distinct from generated fixtures; any isolated dependency alignment is disclosed and must preserve assertions/inventory/coverage.
implementation_acceptance_risks: Native pytest critical-hook/worker bootstrap and Vitest public experimental reporter/worker identity behavior require actual pinned subprocess evidence; no tests ran during design.
Cooperative groups cannot contain arbitrary malicious or unobserved daemonized descendants. Observed escape retains uncertainty/charge; no PID-based reaper signals.
No actual macOS lifecycle, installer, filesystem or runner matrix has run; M4 cannot claim cross-platform completion without it.
Independent apispec and tailwind-merge are research candidates, not completed adoption. The latter requires a disclosed derivative dependency alignment or a replacement matching candidate.
Local security tools are absent. Pinned scanners must demonstrate sensitivity; a reported Gitleaks issue means a zero exit alone is not evidence.
Performance targets and quotas are contracts to measure, not current speed or security claims.
release_gates: Opus design review and required repairs before source implementation.
Real native runner, crash/signal/resource/selection/privacy/doctor and bounded-state acceptance across A1-A14.
Independent adoption, actual Linux and macOS matrix, security sensitivity/passing gates and specified performance samples.
Integrated Opus audit, independent Astra audit and reverified Sol corrections when needed.
Separate user license, distribution-name, publication, main merge and live installation decisions.
documentation_checks: Read approved product/context, earlier review dispositions, interoperability and runner/scheduler research.
Inspected legacy bootstrap/config/test/install and read-only provisional candidate patterns.
Checked task ownership, shared signature consistency, placeholder terms, A1-A14 and all eight security axes.
JSON parse and git diff --check; source tests deliberately not run for docs-only changes.
